bev.name: Bev
bev.plays: Tennis (doubles only, I'm not a masochist)
bev.short: Thursday social organiser since 2019. Keeper of the clipboard. Has strong opinions about tramlines.
bev.bio: I started organising our Thursday night social tennis because nobody else would, and five years later nobody else still will. I've got two grown-up kids, one dog who steals balls, and a forehand my coach describes as 'enthusiastic'. I write here mostly so I can stop explaining the same things in the WhatsApp group.

dan.name: Dan
dan.plays: Tennis on Saturdays, padel when someone drags me
dan.short: 34. Intermediate forever. Ran the club ladder off a spreadsheet for seven months and lived to tell the tale.
dan.bio: Accountant by day, 3.5 by night (on a good night, with a following wind). I'm in that bit of the club where you're too good for the beginners' social and nowhere near good enough for the team, so I spend most of my life trying to find a game. This blog is a cry for help with paragraph breaks.

priya.name: Priya
priya.plays: Padel and tennis, both badly, both happily
priya.short: Picked up a racket in July. Have apologised more times than I've hit a winner.
priya.bio: I joined my local club this summer after my friend promised padel was 'basically just tennis in a box'. It is not. I'm documenting my first year as a racket sports person so future beginners know it's normal to feel like a ball machine has a personal grudge against you.
interests: not getting hit by a volley

graham.name: Graham
graham.plays: Squash, and tennis when my knees allow
graham.short: Retired. Squash section secretary. Has sat through more committee meetings about booking software than any man should.
graham.bio: Forty years of squash, eleven on the club committee, and a working knowledge of every booking system that has ever crashed on a Sunday morning. My wife says I should take up golf. I say golf is just squash for people who've given up. I write here when the committee minutes aren't enough of an outlet.

terry.name: Terry
terry.plays: Tennis coach (LTA Level 3), reluctant padel coach
terry.short: Tennis coach for 22 years. Has opinions about pickleball, padel, ball machines and parents. Mostly the same opinion.
terry.bio: I've coached tennis at the club since before half the members were born. I run the junior squads, the Monday cardio tennis and, since the committee 'had a vision', padel beginners on a Wednesday. I don't do social media. Bev said this isn't social media. I'm not convinced.

mel.name: Mel
mel.plays: Pickleball and tennis coach, padel whenever there's a court
mel.short: Tennis AND pickleball coach. Thinks every racket sport is the best racket sport. Overuses capitals.
mel.bio: I coach tennis and pickleball at the club and run our Saturday pickleball drop-in, which has gone from 6 people to 40 in a year!! I genuinely think anyone can play a racket sport and have a brilliant time if someone just gets them on court and stops them worrying. Terry and I disagree about almost everything. It's fine. Mostly.

malcolm.name: Malcolm
malcolm.plays: Tennis, badly, in the over-60s B team
malcolm.short: Club chair. Writes as he speaks at the AGM: briefly, and with a sigh.
malcolm.bio: Chair of the club since a vote nobody else stood in. Before that, treasurer, which explains a lot. I play doubles in the over-60s B team and serve underarm when my shoulder says so. I have been asked to contribute to this blog. I am contributing.

jake.name: Jake
jake.plays: Social tennis, plus whatever the club has a court free for
jake.short: Designer and developer, member at a big multi-sport club in Surrey. Accidentally built an app because of a WhatsApp group.
jake.bio: I run a small design and development studio and play social tennis at a club in Surrey. A couple of years ago I got fed up of watching our social organiser juggle a secret spreadsheet, so I built a little tool to do the pairings. It turned into Rallio. Bev made me write a post about it. I'm the only one on here using my real name, which means I can't hide my double faults.
